ls.title: Craft that begins with the soil.
ls.short: Living soil is a growing method that uses a biologically active soil environment, where microbes, fungi and organic matter interact.
ls.p1: Living soil is a growing method that uses a biologically active soil environment, where microbes, fungi and organic matter interact.
ls.p2: At GOKURAKU we look not only at the plant itself, but also at the soil environment that supports its roots.
ls.p3: Preparing the soil, observing every day, managing water. We value each step of growing.
ls.dia.title: What happens in the soil
ls.dia.1.d: Organic matter such as fallen leaves is supplied to the surface and inside of the soil.
ls.dia.2.d: Microbes and fungi gradually break down the organic matter.
ls.dia.3.d: What is broken down becomes nutrients the plant can use.
ls.dia.4.d: The plant takes up nutrients from the soil through its roots.
ls.dia.note: This diagram explains how soil works. It does not guarantee the safety or quality of any product, or compare it with others.

cr.title: Japanese craftsmanship. That care, in every step.
cr.p1: From checking the growing environment to finishing after harvest.
cr.p2: At GOKURAKU, we value the steps our Japanese staff are involved in.
cr.p3: We observe the plants and check each one carefully. Spending time and effort even on steps no one sees is the foundation of how we work.
st.label: Four quality steps
st.1.d: We prepare soil where microbes can live.
st.1.more: Details of the soil, materials and methods we use will be posted here once confirmed.
st.2.d: We check each plant every day, watching watering and the growing environment.
st.2.more: What we record (such as temperature and humidity) will be posted here once confirmed.
st.3.d: We decide when to harvest based on each plant, and trim every flower by hand.
st.3.more: Details of post-harvest handling (such as drying and curing) will be posted here once confirmed.
st.4.d: Details of lot control, visual checks and testing will be posted here once records are in place.
st.4.more: We never publish figures for anything that has not been tested.
